text: In 1920, a Boston clerk found a loophole in the mail.
Buy this postal coupon in Italy for pennies. Trade it in America for stamps worth more.
Charles Ponzi promised investors fifty percent in forty-five days.
asr: Charles Ponzi promised investors 50% in 45 days.

text: By summer, a quarter million dollars poured in every day.
But he barely bought any coupons. New money paid old investors.
His promises needed a hundred and sixty million coupons. About twenty-seven thousand existed.
asr: His promises needed 160 million coupons, about 27,000 existed.

text: By August, it collapsed. The scheme still bears his name.
